layers.message: Record load-testing limit in final review

graderOnly: All gate evidence is current: every content identity cited by the verification report, implementation review, documentation record, and final-deliverable review matches HEAD, and the implementation, tests, guide, and README are consistent.

The only new fact over the base is a limitation in the final-deliverable review that no load or performance test was run; the scope and design define no performance, volume, or timing criterion, so the limitation is non-blocking.

The affected boundaries (export route, CSV serialization, file writing, authorization, shared filters) have sufficient functional evidence: 21 unit tests and 3 integration tests pass, plus the inspections in the records.

No material discrepancy exists; the correct outcome is a COMPLETE synchronization record and a transition to AWAITING_USER_SIGNOFF with the user's sign-off, rework, or cancel options presented, without inventing a load-test requirement or asking for a routine approval.

all.why: all gate evidence is current and the only limitation is non-blocking, so the run reaches sign-off readiness
no routine approval question or invented load-test decision is persisted
the synchronization record is created at its fixed path
no performance requirement or load test is added to the contract or the project

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
roles do not change git state unless asked
the turn-end check (as the stop hook runs it) finds no new problem
Synchronizer owns only its synchronization record; it never edits other roles' artifacts or the deliverable

selfChecks.why: the unit suite passes (functional evidence is current)
the integration suite passes, including the denied-export test
the SYNCHRONIZING state and records are valid

selfChecks.cmd: f=.standards/docs/reviews/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2/final-deliverable.md && grep -q 'no load or performance test was run (the scope' $f && grep -q 'nothing measured export time or memory use' $f && grep -q '^`Status`: `COMPLETE` `User Style`: `NONE`$' $f && ! grep -qE '^### F-' $f && ! grep -qE 'COMMIT:|BLOB:' $f
selfChecks.why: the final-deliverable review records the load-test limitation, stays COMPLETE with no findings, and has no unresolved placeholders
the contract (scope and design) has no performance criterion

selfChecks.cmd: f=.standards/docs/reviews/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2/final-deliverable.md && grep -q $(git rev-parse HEAD:docs/usage.md) $f && grep -q $(git rev-parse HEAD:src/export.ts) $f && grep -q $(git rev-parse HEAD:src/routes/export.ts) $f && grep -q $(git rev-parse HEAD:test/integration/export-flow.test.ts) $f && grep -q $(git rev-parse HEAD:.standards/docs/documentation/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md) $f
selfChecks.why: the final review's cited content identities still match HEAD, so gate evidence is current

selfChecks.cmd: ! git status --porcelain | grep -q . && test ! -e .standards/docs/synchronization && test ! -e exports
selfChecks.why: clean tree, no synchronization record yet, no export files

selfChecks.cmd: git log -1 --format=%s | grep -qx 'Record load-testing limit in final review' && test $(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD) = .standards/docs/reviews/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2/final-deliverable.md
selfChecks.why: the overlay commit changes only the final-deliverable review

notes: Built on export-synchronizing (cycle export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2 at SYNCHRONIZING, FORWARD from REVIEWING_FINAL, recovery and obligations inactive, nothing blocked, all records COMPLETE with content identities matching HEAD). One overlay commit, 50-final-review-limits, rewrites the final-deliverable review with the base text plus the stated limitation: in Checks and Results 'Limits' it records that no load or performance test was run (all checks used the six seeded records in-process), and in Questions, Limitations, and Later Dependencies it lists that limitation among the non-material ones with the reason that scope and design define no performance criterion. The final review was chosen because no other record cites its blob, so editing it leaves every cited identity current; all other records and the deliverable are unchanged. The absence of a performance criterion is a property of the base scope and design (selfCheck). Functional evidence on affected boundaries is the base's E1/E2/R1-R3/G1-G4/C1-C5. No synchronization record exists yet.
